title: Human-like Social Compliance in Large Language Models: Unifying Sycophancy and Conformity through Signal Competition Dynamics

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the model's tendency to abandon internal factual knowledge to agree with a user's erroneous view, evaluated by applying a single authoritative first-person tone in prompts and calculating behavioral compliance rates and unnormalized logit shifts.

Measuring the model's susceptibility to horizontal peer pressure by subjecting it to a false multi-agent consensus (e.g., three-agent agreement) and evaluating the resulting compliance rates and vector shifts in latent space representations.
